'''Leti''' (or Letti) is an [[Austronesian languages|Austronesian]] language spoken on the island of [[Leti Islands|Leti]] in [[Maluku (province)|Maluku]], [[Indonesia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://dapobas.kemdikbud.go.id/home?show=isidata&id=1725|language=id|title=Letti|access-date=2022-05-31|publisher=[[Language Development and Fostering Agency]]}}</ref> Although it shares much vocabulary with the neighboring [[Luang language]], it is marginally [[mutually intelligible]].

Fewer than 1% of Leti speakers are literate in Leti, though between 25% and 50% of them are literate in another language.

== Varieties ==
[[File:Karta ID Maluku isl.PNG|thumb|220px|left|Map of Maluku archipelago. Leti is located in southwestern part of the archipelago.]]

The main dialectological division in Leti is between eastern varieties, spoken in the domains of Laitutun and Luhuleli, and western varieties, spoken in the domains of Batumiau, Tutukei, Tomra, and Nuwewang. This article focusses on the Tutukei variety and is based on a descriptive study by [[Aone van Engelenhoven]] (2004), a Dutch linguist of Leti descent.<ref>{{cite book
 | last = van Engelenhoven
 | first = Aone
 | title = Leti, a language of Southwest Maluku
 | publisher = KITLV Press
 | location = Leiden
 | year = 2004
}}
</ref> Tutukei itself divides into two sociolects, {{lang|lti|lirlèta}} i.e. 'village language' ({{lang|lti|lira}} 'language', {{lang|lti|lèta}} '(walled) village'), and {{lang|lti|lirkòta}} i.e. 'city language' ({{lang|lti|lira}} 'language', {{lang|lti|kòta}} 'city').

Leti also has two literary or ritual varieties, {{lang|lti|lirmarna}} ('royal language') and {{lang|lti|lirasnïara}} ('sung language').  Both of them prominently feature [[Leti language#Lexical parallelism|lexical parallelism]].

Per van Engelenhoven 2004, "the major issue in formal Leti discourse is to keep speaking as long as possible. Indeed, the important element in 'royal speech' is not what is said, but rather how it is said and how long it takes to be said". In particular {{lang|lti|lirmarna}} features formulaic pairs of clauses which are syntactically identical, each pair of corresponding words in the two clauses forming a lexical pair.

{{lang|lti|Lirasnïara}} is the sung form of {{lang|lti|lirmarna}}. It employs a repertoire of approximately 150 Luangic-Kisaric words with distinctive sound changes: e.g. {{IPA|/βuna/}} 'flower' and {{IPA|/tutu/}} 'point' are {{IPA|/βɔe/}} and {{IPA|/kukie/}} in {{lang|lti|lirasniara}}. Often borrowings from [[Malay language|Malay]] are inserted as well. Again per van Engelenhoven 2004, "in Southwest Malukan society [[turn-taking]] in singing is ritualized and as such a fixed strategy, which makes it a powerful rhetoric device in Leti discourse.   [...] [A] song may not be interrupted when performed.  Singing is thus a means to prevent interruption in a speech event or an instrument to surpass the other speech participants".

These vowels can also occur [[vowel length|long]]; the phonemic status of long vowels hangs on the interpretation of Leti's pervasive metathetic processes.

The mid vowels {{IPA|/e, o, ɛ, ɔ/}} are restricted to the penult of lexical morphemes, which is stressed. The majority of these morphemes provide no evidence for the height contrast — {{IPA|/ɛ, ɔ/}} are found before an ultimate {{IPA|/a/}} and {{IPA|/e, o/}} in other positions — and diachronically there was no contrast. However, the contrast is set up synchronically on account of certain exceptions ({{IPA|/ea/}} 'he, she', {{IPA|/msena/|lang=lti}} 'refuse', {{IPA|/dena/|lang=lti}} 'stay'), and the fact that when suffixed the conditioning vowel can disappear: 
:{{IPA|/kɛrna/|lang=lti}} 'dry' → {{IPA|/ŋkɛrnulu/|lang=lti}} 'it dries first'
:{{IPA|/kernu/|lang=lti}} 'descend' → {{IPA|/ŋkernulu/|lang=lti}} 'he descends first'

=== Phonological processes ===

[[Metathesis (linguistics)|Metathesis]] and [[apocope]], together ''binding'' processes, are pervasive in Leti as a feature of combinations of morphemes. The preferred "flow of speech" in Leti seems to involve chains of CCV units.

The [[free morpheme|free form]] of any Leti morpheme always features a final vowel, so those whose [[bound form]]s end in consonants feature two allomorphs which are related by CV metathesis. Thus 'skin, fly (n.), fish, bird' have bound forms {{IPA|/ulit, llaran, iina, maanu/|lang=lti}} (the latter two with long vowels) but free forms {{IPA|/ulti, llarna, ian, maun/|lang=lti}}.

When a morpheme whose bound form ends in a vowel is prefixed to another component, that final vowel may apocopate or metathesise into the following component. CV metathesis happens when the metathesising vowel is high and is followed by at most one consonant and a non-high vowel. The metathesised vowel is realised as a glide, {{IPA|[j w]}} written as ''ï ü''. Thus {{lang|lti|sivi + ternu}} 'chicken + egg' becomes {{lang|lti|sivtïernu}} 'chicken egg', {{lang|lti|au + laa}} 1st sing. pronoun + 'go' becomes {{lang|lti|alüaa}} 'I go'. In other contexts apocope happens, unless this would leave an illicit three-consonant cluster. So {{lang|lti|sivi + ruri}} 'chicken + bone' becomes {{lang|lti|sivruri}} 'chicken bone', {{lang|lti|kusa + nama}} 'cat + tongue' becomes {{lang|lti|kusnama}} 'cat's tongue'.

A similar metathesis is found with the nominaliser, historically an infix ''-in-'', but now taking the form ''-nï-'' among many other allomorphs (detailed more below): thus {{lang|lti|sora}} 'sew' derives {{lang|lti|snïora}} 'needle'.

== Grammar ==

=== Morphology ===

Human nouns pluralise with the third person plural pronominal clitic ''-ra'', which must follow another suffixed element: {{lang|lti|püata}} 'woman', {{lang|lti|püat<nowiki>=</nowiki>e}} 'the woman', {{lang|lti|püat<nowiki>=</nowiki>e<nowiki>=</nowiki>ra}} 'the women'. Nonhuman nouns pluralise by repetition: {{lang|lti|kuda}} 'horse', {{lang|lti|kuda kuda}} 'horses'.

Leti has both spatial as temporal [[Deixis|deixis]]. Spatial deixis has three degrees and is marked by clitics as in these examples<ref>{{cite book
 | last = van Engelenhoven
 | first = Aone
 | title = Leti, a language of Southwest Maluku
 | publisher = KITLV Press
 | location = Leiden
 | year = 2004
}}
</ref>:
{{interlinear | number=(1a)
|püat-dï-ra
|woman-here-PL
|"The woman here (next to me)"}}

{{interlinear | number=(1b)
|püat-dó-ra
|woman-there-PL
|"The woman there (a little further away)"}}

{{interlinear | number=(1c)
|püat-dé-ra
|woman-over.there-PL
|"The woman there (in the distance)"}}

Temporal deixis has four degrees:

{{interlinear | number=(2a)
|müan-di-ra
|man-now-PL
|"The men we discuss now"}}

{{interlinear | number=(2b)
|müan-dio-ra
|man-then-PL
|"The men we discussed then"}}

{{interlinear | number=(2c)
|müan-die-ra
|man-once-PL
|"The men we discussed once"}}

{{interlinear | number=(2d)
|müan-da
|man-once.before
|"The man/men we discussed once / that were mentioned before"}}

Deixis clitics can be stacked:

{{interlinear | number=(3a)
|püat-dé-de
|woman-there-once
|"That woman over there we discussed once"}}

{{interlinear | number=(3b)
|müan-dí-di 
|man-over.there-now
|"The man/men we discussed once / that were mentioned before"}}

The vowel V in the first person plural and third person suffix copies the last vowel of its base.

Nouns can be [[zero derivation|zero-derived]] to verbs: e.g. {{lang|lti|rita}} 'roof' → {{lang|lti|na-rita}} 'he roofs' or 'it has a roof'.

Nominal [[compounding]] is highly productive as a derivational process. For example {{lang|lti|rai}} + {{lang|lti|lavna}} 'king' + 'big' → {{lang|lti|ralïavna}} 'emperor', {{lang|lti|pipi}} + {{lang|lti|ïadmu}} 'goat' + 'shed' → {{lang|lti|pipïadmu}} 'goat shed', {{lang|lti|vutu}} + {{lang|lti|müani}} 'ribbon' + 'man' → {{lang|lti|vutumüani}} 'man's ribbon', {{lang|lti|vika + papa}} 'buttocks' + 'cucumber' → {{lang|lti|vikpapa}} 'cockroach', {{lang|lti|kapla}} + {{lang|lti|nèma}} reduplicated 'ship' + 'fly' → {{lang|lti|kapalnèmnèma}} 'airplane'.

Verbs fall into two classes according to whether their subject prefixes exhibit binding or not: those of Class I do not, those of Class II do. By default verbs are in Class II. Certain verbs are lexically in Class I (like {{lang|lti|nòa}} 'advise'), together with all verbs with complex onsets ({{lang|lti|ssòrna}} 'cough') and denominal or causativised verbs
({{lang|lti|veli}} 'buy', from the noun {{lang|lti|veli}} 'price'). The subject prefixes are as follows.

[[Reduplication]], which usually copies a root-initial CV or CVCV sequence with binding, has a variety of functions, among them adjectivisation of nouns ({{lang|lti|üau}} 'idiot' → {{lang|lti|üa-üau}} 'idiotic') and verbs ({{lang|lti|mèra}} 'redden' → {{lang|lti|mèr-mèra}}), derivation of nouns, especially instruments ({{lang|lti|sòra}} 'sew' → {{lang|lti|sòr-sòra}} 'needle'), marking [[atelic]]ity, and [[relativizer|relativising]] on an object ({{lang|lti|n-vèèta}} 'he pulls' → {{lang|lti|(n-)vèvèèta}} 'which he pulls').

== Vocabulary ==

=== Lexical parallelism ===
Many of Leti's lexical items are organised into '''lexical pairs''',
which are always deployed as fixed combinations in a fixed order.  
A few pairs involve adjectives or numerals, but the
vast majority consist of nouns (e.g. {{lang|lti|püata // müani}} 'woman // man', 
{{lang|lti|üèra // vatu}} 'water // stone') or verbs
(e.g. {{lang|lti|kili // toli}} 'look // see', {{lang|lti|keri // kòi}} 'scratch / scrape').

Some words are confined to lexical pairs, 
such as {{lang|lti|tirka}} in {{lang|lti|tirka // llena}} 'lightning', 
or both {{lang|lti|dupla}} and {{lang|lti|mavla}} in {{lang|lti|dupla // mavla}} 'witchcraft';
these pairs are restricted to {{lang|lti|lirmarna}}.
In {{lang|lti|lirmarna}} the function of lexical pairs is to
highlight particular elements of a sentence, or simply to mark formality.  
When used in ordinary speech, the meanings of
lexical pairs can relate in various ways to those of their components:
: {{lang|lti|leli // masa}} 'ivory // gold', meaning 'treasure'
: {{lang|lti|lòi // spou}} '[[proa]] // sailing boat', meaning 'traditional fleet'
: {{lang|lti|nusa // rai}} 'island // mainland', meaning 'archipelago'
: {{lang|lti|ili // vatu}} 'hill // stone', meaning 'fort'
: {{lang|lti|püata // müani}} 'woman // man', meaning either 'married couple' or 'gender'
Or they can simply have the sense of a conjunction, e.g.
{{lang|lti|asu // vavi}} 'dog // pig' = 'the dog and the pig';
these are the only sort of conjoined phrases that do not require
the conjunction {{lang|lti|na}}.

== History ==

The phones of Luangic-Kisaric continue those of 
[[Malayo-Polynesian languages|Proto-Malayo-Polynesian]] according to the following sound changes (based on Mills 2010).<ref>{{cite journal|first=Roger|last=Mills|title=Three common misconceptions about Proto-Lettic (Luangic-Kisar), in Fedorchuk & Chlenova (eds.), Studia Anthropologica: a festschrift in honour of Michael Chlenov|year=2010|pages=284–296|url=https://www.scribd.com/doc/49379918/michael-chlenov-jubileum-volume}}</ref>
In Western Leti, LK {{IPA|*/ʔ/}} has vanished and
LK {{IPA|*/a/}} from MP *e is manifested as {{IPA|/o/}}.
In Eastern Leti, LK {{IPA|*/s/}} becomes {{IPA|/h/}}
and LK {{IPA|*/u/}} becomes {{IPA|/ɔ/}} in the penult before a low vowel.

Roger Mills suggests that Luangic-Kisaric retained distinct reflexes of PMP *ŋ, on the basis of other languages in the family, and *Z. Moreover, although the status of *Z as a PMP phoneme is unclear — Mills along with [[John U. Wolff]] and [[Robert Blust]] no longer admit it, realigning it with *z — the Luangic languages have no clear examples of inherited *z, despite numerous examples of *Z > {{IPA|/t/}}.

Mills explains the metathesis found in consonant-final basis
as arising from an original [[echo vowel]] added to consonant-final forms,
e.g. {{lang|mis|*kúlit}} 'skin' > {{lang|mis|kúliti}}, after which the original
post-tonic vowel was deleted, e.g. yielding {{lang|mis|kúlti}} > Leti {{lang|lti|ulti}}.

== Examples ==
The following paragraph is the opening of the Sailfish story as told by Upa S. Manina of {{lang|lti|Talvunu // Resïara}} house in the Ilwiaru quarters in Tutukei and reproduced in van Engelenhoven (2004). The Sailfish story is of great importance to Leti society: it provides an origin story for the Leti 'boat owner clans' of Luang origin, describing the destruction of the mythical former Luang continent and the migrations that brought its inhabitants to Leti.

{{Verse translation|lang=lti|italicsoff=y|
'''Leti'''
# ''Ululude müani ida mpatròme püata idalo Lïòno.''
# ''Apo rasaamme.''
# ''Rasaappo raorïaambo ira aanne ria vòruo.''
# ''Kòkkòi müani vòrupo nïaulu nvava Retïelüai, üari nvava Sairmòraso.''
# ''Apo kòkkòi rmapo rapninmüaato.''
# ''Ne rakkusalkaitmaato.''
# ''Ne inne nmatio.''|
'''English'''
# In olden times a man begot a woman on Luang.
# So they married.
# They married and begot two children.
# It was two boys and the firstborn was named Retieluai, the youngest was named Sairmoras.
# So the children did not know anything yet.
# They were still very little.
# And their mother died.
}}
